name: Push-Up
short_description: Fundamental upper-body pushing exercise developing chest, shoulder, and triceps strength while reinforcing trunk stability.
instructions: Set your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart on the floor with fingers spread.
Extend your legs behind you with feet together, creating a rigid straight line from head to heels.
Engage your glutes and brace your core to prevent sagging in the lumbar spine.
Lower your chest with control until it hovers roughly 2 inches above the floor, keeping elbows angled at roughly 45 degrees to your torso.
Press powerfully through your palms to return to the starting position without locking elbows aggressively.
form_cues: Keep neck neutral by focusing eyes 12 inches ahead of your fingertips.
Screw your hands into the floor to activate external shoulder rotators.
Maintain a rigid plank throughout the entire range of motion.
Do not flare elbows out wide at 90 degrees.
common_mistakes: Sagging hips due to disengaged core or glutes.
Flaring elbows excessively, increasing anterior shoulder impingement risk.
Shortening range of motion by bobbing the head rather than lowering the chest.
breathing: Inhale deeply on the descent (eccentric phase); exhale forcefully through pursed lips as you drive up through the concentric phase.

name: Bodyweight Squat
short_description: Essential lower-body compound movement training knee extension, hip flexion, and pelvic control without external load.
instructions: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned slightly outward at roughly 15 to 30 degrees.
Extend your arms forward for counterbalance or clasp your hands at chest height.
Initiate the descent by breaking simultaneously at the hips and knees, sitting back and down.
Descend until your hip crease is parallel to or slightly below the top of your knees while keeping your chest proud.
Drive through mid-foot and heel to return to a standing position, squeezing glutes at the top.
form_cues: Track knees directly in line with your second and third toes.
Keep heels glued to the floor throughout the entire movement.
Maintain a tall, upright torso with an engaged core.
common_mistakes: Knees caving inward (valgus collapse) upon ascent.
Lifting heels off the ground due to limited ankle dorsiflexion.
Rounding the lower back in the bottom hole (butt wink).
breathing: Inhale and brace your abdominal wall as you descend; exhale smoothly as you drive out of the bottom position.

name: Glute Bridge
short_description: Targeted posterior chain drill activating the glutes and training hip extension while minimizing spinal load.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet planted flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Position your heels approximately 6 to 8 inches away from your buttocks.
Rest your arms flat along your sides with palms facing down.
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to elevate your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold the top contraction for 1 to 2 seconds before lowering under control to just above the floor.
form_cues: Drive the movement from the hips and glutes, not the lumbar spine.
Tuck your pelvis slightly under (posterior pelvic tilt) at lockout.
Avoid hyperextending your lower back at peak extension.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back excessively instead of engaging glutes.
Pushing from toes rather than driving through the heels.
Rushing repetitions without establishing peak contraction.
breathing: Inhale as you lower your hips toward the floor; exhale and contract glutes forcefully as you thrust upward.

name: Plank
short_description: Foundational isometric anti-extension core drill building structural trunk endurance and lumbar protection.
instructions: Place your forearms flat on the floor with elbows aligned directly under your shoulders.
Extend your legs straight back with toes tucked, rising up onto balls of your feet.
Engage your core, tighten your quads, and squeeze your gluteal muscles.
Maintain a straight, horizontal line from head to ankles without dipping or piking your hips.
Hold the isometric contraction for the prescribed duration while maintaining continuous steady breathing.
form_cues: Pull elbows isometrically toward your toes to maximize abdominal recruitment.
Gaze down at the floor between your wrists to preserve cervical spine neutrality.
Actively push the floor away to keep shoulder blades from collapsing.
common_mistakes: Sagging lumbar spine due to core fatigue.
Piking hips upwards toward the ceiling to relieve tension.
Holding breath during the static hold.
breathing: Breathe rhythmically in through the nose and out through the mouth while maintaining 360-degree core pressure.

name: Reverse Lunge
short_description: Unilateral lower-body movement addressing strength imbalances, knee stability, and single-leg balance.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands placed on your hips or in front of your chest.
Take a controlled step backward with your right leg, landing on the ball of the foot.
Lower your hips vertically until both front and rear knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Ensure front knee stays stacked directly over front ankle without collapsing inward.
Drive through the front heel and midfoot to return cleanly to the starting standing position, then alternate legs.
form_cues: Maintain a slight forward torso lean to keep tension loaded on the working front hip.
Control the descent so the back knee gently taps or hovers 1 inch above the mat.
Keep hips square to the front wall throughout.
common_mistakes: Letting the lead knee collapse medial to the foot.
Slamming the rear knee into the hard ground.
Pushing off the rear toe rather than driving through the front working leg.
breathing: Inhale as you step back and lower into the lunge; exhale as you press off the lead foot to step forward.

name: Barbell Bench Press
short_description: The gold-standard upper-body compound barbell exercise for developing maximal pressing strength and pectoral hypertrophy.
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes aligned directly beneath the racked barbell.
Plant feet firmly into the floor, retract shoulder blades, and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the barbell with straight arms and settle it directly over your mid-chest.
Lower the barbell under control in a slight diagonal arc to touch the mid-to-lower sternum.
Press the barbell back up explosively to the starting locked-out position over your shoulders.
form_cues: Retract and depress scapulae to create a stable pressing shelf.
Tuck elbows at a 45-to-75 degree angle relative to your torso.
Drive through your legs (leg drive) to anchor your lower body.
common_mistakes: Flaring elbows out to 90 degrees, loading excessive shearing stress onto the anterior shoulder capsule.
Bouncing the bar violently off the sternum.
Lifting hips off the bench during heavy attempts.
breathing: Take a deep diaphragmatic breath and brace at the top; lower the bar with control; exhale forcefully as you press through the sticking point.

name: Lat Pulldown
short_description: Primary vertical pulling exercise that develops upper-back width, lat activation, and scapular downward rotation.
instructions: Adjust the thigh pad securely so your knees are locked firmly under the rollers with feet flat.
Reach up and grasp the wide bar with a pronated (overhand) grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Sit down under the pad with torso upright and a slight natural arch in your upper spine.
Initiate the pull by depressing your scapulae, drawing elbows down and back toward your ribcage until the bar touches your upper chest.
Control the eccentric return, allowing the bar to rise back up until your arms and lats achieve a full overhead stretch.
form_cues: Drive the pull with your elbows, imagining pulling through your pinky fingers.
Keep chest lifted toward the bar throughout the repetition.
Avoid swinging your entire upper torso backward to gain momentum.
common_mistakes: Excessive torso lean and using lumbar momentum to heave the load down.
Pulling the bar behind the neck, placing dangerous stress on the cervical spine and rotator cuff.
Shortening the top stretch range.
breathing: Exhale as you pull the bar down to your collarbone; inhale smoothly as you control the cable back up to the top stretch.

name: Leg Press
short_description: High-volume lower-body machine movement isolating quad and glute development while supporting the back on a fixed sled.
instructions: Sit back firmly into the machine with your back and head supported flush against the backrest.
Place your feet shoulder-width apart in the center of the sled platform with toes angled slightly outward.
Disengage the safety levers while maintaining full control of the weight carriage.
Lower the sled with control by bending your knees until they form an angle of approximately 90 degrees.
Drive powerfully through the platform with your mid-foot and heels to return to the top without hyper-extending or locking out knees.
form_cues: Keep lower back and sacrum firmly pinned against the back pad at all times.
Track knees outward in line with your toes throughout the descent and ascent.
Stop 2 degrees short of full knee lockout to preserve joint integrity and maintain constant muscle tension.
common_mistakes: Allowing pelvis to curl off the backrest (lumbar flexion) at maximum depth.
Violently locking out knees at the top of the press.
Placing feet too low on the platform, causing knees to drift excessively past toes and lifting heels.
breathing: Inhale as you allow the sled to descend toward your chest; exhale forcefully as you drive the sled upward.

name: Seated Cable Row
short_description: Horizontal pulling cable movement building upper-back thickness, posture correction, and scapular retraction control.
instructions: Sit on the bench facing the low pulley and place your feet firmly on the footrests with knees slightly flexed.
Reach forward with a neutral spine to grasp the V-bar handle, then slide back into an upright starting posture.
With arms fully extended and shoulders protracted, brace your core.
Pull the handle toward your lower abdomen/belly button by retracting your scapulae and driving elbows straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at peak contraction for 1 second, then control the handle forward into a deep lat stretch.
form_cues: Keep torso nearly upright (80–90 degrees) with minimal backward rocking.
Initiate the pull by pulling shoulder blades back, not by bending the arms first.
Keep elbows close to your torso during the row.
common_mistakes: Rocking the entire torso back and forth like a rowing boat to move the weight.
Rounding the lower and thoracic back during the eccentric reach.
Shrugging shoulders up into the ears at peak contraction.
breathing: Exhale as you pull the attachment toward your abdomen; inhale deeply as you guide the weight back to the starting stretch.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
short_description: Guided overhead pressing machine targeting the deltoids with maximum stability and minimal stabilization risk.
instructions: Adjust seat height so the machine handles sit at approximately ear to collarbone level.
Sit tall with your back and head firmly supported by the backrest, feet planted shoulder-width on the floor.
Grip the handles firmly with an overhand or neutral grip and wrists straight.
Press the handles smoothly overhead until arms are extended but not locked out.
Lower the handles under control back to ear level, keeping tension constant on the deltoids.
form_cues: Keep elbows slightly in front of the coronal plane (in the scapular plane).
Avoid arching your lower back away from the back pad.
Do not shrug neck or shoulders into ears at overhead lockout.
common_mistakes: Arching lower spine excessively to turn the exercise into an incline chest press.
Letting the weight stack slam at the bottom of each repetition.
Over-gripping and bending wrists backward under load.
breathing: Exhale as you press the load overhead; inhale smoothly as you control the descent back to starting height.
